question: Can the run-005 voices and Runway's sound effects give episode 1's every line and new action a warm, real sound?
why: M2 is the first time someone else plays. With captions only, the episode is silent where it most needs warmth: Pip's relief, Wick's gruffness, the narrator over the beam. Every new action also needs a sound (look bar).
sameAcrossJobs: Voices through Runway text to speech with the run-005 presets (narrator Wanda, Pip Mabel, Wick Arjun) and the narrator file's model and settings, 1 credit a line. Sound effects through eleven_text_to_sound_v2 at 1 credit a second. Every clip goes through art/voice/chain.mjs in the client.
decideBy: Each clip decodes, and sound effects come back at their requested length.
The client times every beat from the rendered line, and the simulator still finds every path inside 5 to 7 minutes.
The owner judges voices and mix on the Quest's speakers.
learnEvenIfRejected: How the three run-005 voices carry a whole episode, and how long real lines run against the caption estimate.
reusableOutput: Episode 1's prepared lines, and foley for objects, the drawer, the page and the satchel that every later episode reuses.
capNote: One credit per line plus a credit per second of foley: 109. The cap is the 120 quoted to the owner, leaving room to redo about ten clips.

soundJobs.use: a dropped lantern rolls to the edge
soundJobs.promptText: A small brass lantern dropped onto a wooden floor, a soft metal clink, then it rolls a short way and stops. Close, dry, quiet.
A small candle flame catching and flaring up inside a glass lantern, a soft whoomp and a gentle crackle. Close and quiet, no hiss.

soundJobs.use: something set down on a page
soundJobs.promptText: A small light object set down gently on thick paper, one soft papery tap. Close, quiet.
A single thick storybook page turned slowly by hand, a full soft paper sweep and settle. Close, quiet, no rustling crowd.
A small paper kite caught by a gust and lifted, a soft fluttering whoosh of wind and paper. Gentle, airy, no howling.

soundJobs.use: a little wooden ladder laid across and crawled over
soundJobs.promptText: A small wooden ladder laid down on stone with a gentle knock, then soft wooden creaks as something small crawls across it. Close, quiet.
A thin thread pulled taut and plucked once, a tiny soft twang. Close and quiet.

soundJobs.use: a rope thrown across and pulled
soundJobs.promptText: A coil of rough rope thrown across a short gap, a soft swish and a thump as it lands, then a creak as it pulls tight. Close, quiet.

soundJobs.use: a spark rising up to the lighthouse lamp
soundJobs.promptText: A single tiny spark drifting upward, a faint delicate shimmering crackle rising in pitch. Very soft, magical, no music.
A large old oil lamp catching light behind glass, a warm soft whoomp and a low gentle glow hum. Warm, soft, no alarm.

soundJobs.use: a keepsake slipped into a leather satchel
soundJobs.promptText: A small object slipped into a soft leather satchel, a leather flap lifting and falling, and a tiny brass buckle click. Close, quiet.

soundJobs.use: a small wooden drawer slides open
soundJobs.promptText: A small wooden drawer sliding open smoothly on wooden runners, a soft wooden rumble and a gentle stop. Close, quiet.
A small light object lifted from a wooden surface, a tiny soft scrape and tap. Very close, quiet.

soundJobs.use: a small creature takes a gift, pleased
soundJobs.promptText: A tiny soft bright two-note chime, like a small music box, pleased and warm. Very gentle.

soundJobs.use: a small creature turns a gift over, puzzled
soundJobs.promptText: A tiny soft questioning two-note wooden chime, rising, curious. Very gentle.
A soft rustle in dry reeds at night, something small moving nearby. Close, quiet, not scary.

soundJobs.use: a small creature lands from a hop
soundJobs.promptText: A small soft landing thump on sand, gentle. Close, quiet.

voiceJobs.promptText: No, no, no...
It rolled right to the edge. And it's so dark over there.
Could you reach it for me?
It's lit! It was cold, and then you held it, and it just... woke up.
Thank you. I'm not scared now. Well. A bit less.
It's warmer than it's ever been. Like it remembers your hand.
It had never burned so brightly. It was, after all, the first light anyone had ever handed back to him.
Oh! That's kind of you.
But my lantern's still over there, in the dark.
Nobody came. So the little fox took a deep breath, and went to the edge all by himself.
And when he held it close, brave in the dark, the little flame woke up again.
I did it. I really did it!
Wick will be lighting the lamp soon. I'm meant to help him.
Down where the house ends, everything lost drifts home in the end. Buttons. Spoons. Odd socks. And once, a whole umbrella.
Somebody's missing a very big button.
I hope they're not cold without it.
What was that? Who's there?
Only a moth. Moths are never lost. Only distracted.
Moth! You frightened me. And mind your feelers, it's hot!
No, Moth. It isn't for eating. It's for seeing.
See? Out there it's only sand. Dark sand. Nothing to be scared of.
Mostly nothing.
Wick says the lighthouse calls every lost thing home. Every night, round and round.
He says one day it might be my job.
I'd have to stop being scared of the dark first.
The dark didn't say anything. It never does. It only waited, the way it always had, for someone brave enough to walk into it.
Come on, Moth. It's this way. Stay close.
The path went on, and on, and then it simply stopped.
Oh. The lighthouse is right there. I can see the door.
Wick? Wick! He can't hear me from all the way over here.
Maybe if I take a run at it...
No. No, no. Much too far.
It's easy for you, Moth. You've got wings.
Lost things had been falling into that gap for years and years. Far below, the sea kept them.
If only we could cross... Is there anything in that drawer?
A kite? In this wind?
I'm flying! I'm really, actually flying!
Thread! If only someone could carry the end across...
The moth only wanted to be near the light. But it carried the thread across all the same.
A ladder! If I lay it down flat, it's a bridge!
Don't look down. Don't look down. Don't look down.
A sock? It's far too short to reach across.
But it is very warm. Thank you.
Something longer, maybe? Or something that flies?
A key. Maybe the gap is... locked?
Moth, it's not a light, it's a key!
I don't think gaps have keyholes. Is there something to get me over?
Hmm. I don't think this will get me across.
Is there something longer? Or something that flies?
What's all this shouting about? Who's there?
Wick! It's me! I can't get across!
Hmph. Hold still, lad. And catch.
Hand over paw, hand over paw...
You're shaking like a leaf, lad.
I'm fine. I'm fine. Is it always this dark out here?
Every night. That's rather the point of us.
And what do you think you're doing, crossing chasms in the dark?
Someone helped me. Someone very big.
Someone very big? Up there?
They opened the drawer. They just reached in and handed it to me.
Hmph. Well. Thank you kindly, whoever you are.
You should have seen it, Wick. I wasn't even scared. Well. Not very.
Not very, eh? We'll see about that.
Come on then, lad. That lamp won't light itself.
They walked the last of the path together, the old badger and the small fox, toward the dark tower.
Forty years I've lit that lamp. Every single night.
Even when it stormed?
Especially when it stormed.
But tonight the lighthouse stood dark. On a night like this, it had never once been dark.
Can't see the wick to light it. Not like I used to.
Don't you go telling anyone.
I won't. But I've still got my light.
So up they went, a hundred and twelve steps, round and round, to the lamp at the very top.
And the little light became the big one, and swept out over every lost thing in the house.
Not bad, keeper.
Keeper?
Every keeper has a first night. Don't let it go to your head.
Look! It reaches all the way out to you.
Same time tomorrow, keeper?
Same time tomorrow.
Far out in the dark, something lost turned toward the light, and started for home.
And whatever the Reader gave that night, the book kept safe, for another time.
Because lost things, as you'll find, have a way of coming back.
